title: Maximum Subarray
oneLinerQuestion: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Maximum Subarray problem requires finding the contiguous subarray within an integer array that has the largest sum. A brute-force inspection of all possible subarrays takes O(N^2) time. Kadane's Algorithm solves this problem in linear O(N) time through dynamic programming. At each index, we decide whether to add the current element to the existing running subarray or discard the past subarray entirely and start fresh, recognizing that a negative running sum will only detract from any future contiguous sequence.

- Step 1: Accumulator & Maximum Tracking Setup — We initialize two variables: 'maxSum = nums[0]' to store the global maximum contiguous sum found so far, and 'currentSum = 0' to track the running sum of the active candidate subarray.

- Step 2: Linear Subarray Traversal — We iterate through the array element by element from index 0 to nums.length - 1. For each element 'num', we incorporate it into our active candidate window.

- Step 3: Running Sum Accumulation — We add the current number to the running sum: currentSum += num. This represents extending the previous subarray window by one more position.

- Step 4: Global Maximum Evaluation — We compare and update the global tracker: maxSum = Math.max(maxSum, currentSum). This step guarantees that even if subsequent numbers reduce the running sum, our overall peak sum remains safely recorded.

- Step 5: Resetting Negative Prefix Windows — If currentSum drops below 0, any subsequent subarray that appends to it would only have its potential sum diminished. Therefore, we immediately reset: currentSum = 0. This effectively discards the negative prefix and prepares the algorithm to initiate a fresh subarray starting at the next element.

- Step 6: Termination & Return — Once all elements have been processed, the traversal concludes and 'maxSum' is returned as the largest subarray sum.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) because the array is traversed in a single pass of length N. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space as it tracks the answer using only two scalar primitive variables.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxSubArray(nums):
    maxSum = nums[0], currSum = nums[0]
    FOR i FROM 1 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        currSum = MAX(nums[i], currSum + nums[i])
        maxSum = MAX(maxSum, currSum)
    END FOR
    RETURN maxSum
END FUNCTION
